questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: You must slow down and follow instructions from flaggers, signs, and police officers in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take road rage personally. If another driver cuts you off, ignore it and keep driving safely.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if you have a green light. Protect pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Go to the next exit and come back.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving parking spaces, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull over to the side and stop.
Speed up and take the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
Come to a full stop before proceeding when safe.
Drive carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop before proceeding when safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop and let pedestrians and other vehicles pass. Go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Keep extra distance from the vehicle.
Know this driver is less safe because they are distracted.
Not copy this bad driving habit.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused while driving. Avoid distractions like talking to passengers or looking for items. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Makes you sleepy.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces safe driving skills. It makes your reaction time slower and your judgment worse.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to process the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can help you stay awake, but they do not lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: Tailgating is:

options.text: Illegal.
Inconvenient, but nothing more.
The fastest way to get to where you're going.
The best way to let drivers know they aren't driving fast enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Never follow a vehicle too closely. Tailgating is illegal and causes most rear-end crashes. The fine for tailgating can be up to $100.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, stop every two hours for a short break. If you become drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: The most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly, causing a crash.

questions.question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use appropriate headlights. Drive slow enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing a railroad, you should:

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never proceed until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Accelerate to avoid a red light.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Slow to a stop, unless they are already within the intersection.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a stop, unless they are already within the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is about to appear. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. Do not swerve across lanes at the last second to make your exit. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a motor vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver
Only adult passengers
Only passengers under age 16
All occupants in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants in the vehicle
questions.explanation: The law requires everyone in a motor vehicle to wear a safety belt or use a child car seat. Drivers not wearing a safety belt can be fined $25. Passengers age 16 and older not wearing a safety belt can also be fined $25.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.
